table.title: [The Emperor's immediate advisers up to 1911]
table.caption_extra: Up to the present year the Emperor's immediate advisers were:

rows: the Supreme Council of the Empire;
or Grand Council, corresponding to a Privy Council;
which was composed of members of (1) and (2), and Presidents of the Metropolitan Boards.

table.title: [Departments of the Waiwupu (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)]
table.caption_extra: The Ministries. The Waiwupu. Its duties are performed by four departments, viz.—

rows: This department undertakes treaty negotiations with all nations, recommends candidates for the posts of Ministers and Consuls abroad, arranges for the foreign Ministers' and officials' audiences with the Throne, recommends the bestowal of Chinese decorations upon foreign officials and others, and undertakes all foreign negotiations in Peking.

which is charged with the supervision of all foreign interests in railways, mines, telegraphs, manufactures and dockyards, the employment of military or other foreign official, and questions affecting the emigration of coolies and the sending abroad of students. (Many of the functions here enumerated are now in the hands of the Yuchuanpu and the Nungkungshangpu.)

which deals with matters affecting the Customs Tariff, the navigation of steamers in Chinese waters, foreign concessions and loans, and the expenditure of the Ministry itself, and of its Legations and Consulates abroad.
which deals with boundary questions, missionaries, passports, compensation to foreigners, and police and legal questions so far as they concern foreigners.

footnotes: Each of these departments employs about ten under-secretaries and a staff of junior officials.
transcriber_notes: Numbered list of departments printed as run-on paragraphs; split into number / department name / duties, text verbatim (hyphenation at line ends removed).

table.title: [Departments of the Tuchihpu (Ministry of Finance)]
table.caption_extra: The Tuchihpu (Ministry of Finance, formerly Hupu). The Tuchihpu's work is carried on by fourteen separate departments:

rows: the duties of which are to translate and compile books on financial matters, to direct the financial policy of the Empire, and to prepare the national budget.
which is responsible for the preparation and revision of regulations regarding financial matters, and the supply of financial information to the Throne.
which supervises the collection of land taxes, surveys of land, and leases and measurements of property.

which is responsible for receiving the tribute rice from the south, for the inspection of the Imperial granaries in Peking and the provinces, and for the supply of rice to the troops in time of war and to the people in time of famine.
which receives the revenues from the Maritime and Native Customs, and taxes upon wine and tobacco, and supervises the issue of “red” title deeds and Customs passes.
which is in charge of the collection of salt and tea taxes, and the appointment of Provincial Salt Gabelle officials. It also supervises the collection of taxes upon native opium.

which supervises provincial mining enterprises, the transportation of copper from Yunnan and Kueichow, the minting of gold and silver moneys, the printing of Government banknotes and the purchase of copper, bronze and other metals for coinage.
which has the custody of revenue from the provinces as well as tribute in silk and in kind (except grain).
which pays the salaries of princes and other officials inside and outside Peking, and the expenses and victualling of the Army.
which supervises expenditure upon the Army and Navy, the Manchu forces, the “Green” Army and police.
which controls conservancy, dockyard and other Government works.

which inspects all revenue and expenditure of the Empire, and drafts the Budget and estimates. This department is also in charge of the issue of Government bonds and the arrangements for paying foreign indemnities.
which has the custody of gold, silver and copper bullion, coins and paper money.
which receives and dispatches documents and correspondence.

footnotes: The financial schools and colleges are also under the control of the Tuchihpu.
transcriber_notes: Fourteen departments listed, matching the headnote.

Numbered list printed as run-on paragraphs; split into number / department / duties, text verbatim (line-end hyphenation removed; 'bank-notes' broken across a line printed as 'bank- notes', rendered 'banknotes').

table.title: [Departments of the Ministry of Education (Hsüeh Pu)]
table.caption_extra: Ministry of Education (Hsüeh Pu). ...it is divided into five departments, which deal respectively with:

rows: All general business, the preservation of memorials and records, the selection and translation of educational works and the publication of periodicals devoted to education.
The supervision of scientific, literary and musical instruction in universities.
The supervision of primary, middle and high schools.
The supervision of industrial and training schools and institutes.
Finance, the auditing and handling of funds, and the supervision of libraries and other properties of the Ministry.

table.title: [Departments of the Ministry of the Army (Lu Chun-pu)]
table.caption_extra: Ministry of the Army (Lu Chun-pu). ...consists of ten departments, whose duties are respectively:

rows: Administrative, the custody of all documents, supervision of revenue and expenditure and of rewards and punishments of officers.
The preparation of military schemes, revision and issue of military regulations.
General supervision of the military system, and promotion and degradation of officers.
Supplies for the Army and military schools.

transcriber_notes: Ten departments listed, matching the headnote.

table.title: [Departments of the Ministry of the Navy (Hai Chün Pu)]
table.caption_extra: Ministry of the Navy (Hai Chün Pu). ...the work of the Ministry is conducted by a Secretariat of eight members, and nine departments, charged with the following duties:

rows: General administration, control of the movements of naval vessels and general supervision of stores, etc.
Supplies of uniforms, stores and munitions

transcriber_notes: Nine departments listed, matching the headnote. Item 5 printed without a final full stop.

table.title: [Departments of the Ministry of Laws (Fa Pu)]
table.caption_extra: Ministry of Laws (Fa Pu). ...It is divided into nine departments, whose functions are:

rows: The preservation of records, and the preparation of evidence and findings for Imperial consideration; consideration and revision of sentences of the Supreme and Provincial Courts (subject to the confirmation of the Emperor) and the general supervision of administration of civil and criminal law in four provinces and two districts in Mongolia.

Consideration of sentences in Criminal Courts, particularly the preparation of lists of condemned prisoners for the Emperor's consideration each autumn, and the general supervision of administration of criminal and civil law in four provinces and two districts in the Mongolian dependencies (each department exercises this supervision over the administration of law in certain defined portions of the Empire).
The custody of all documents, memorials and dispatches from provincial officials.
Pardons, amnesties and remissions of sentence.
Appointments, promotions and dismissals of provincial judicial officers.
Supervision of gaols under immediate control of the Ministry and in the provinces.
Auditing, receipt and payment of moneys and court fees.
Translation from Chinese into Manchu and vice versa of documents.

transcriber_notes: Headnote on p. 229; the nine items are printed at the head of p. 230. Nine departments listed, matching the headnote. Line-end hyphenation removed.

table.title: [Departments of the Ministry of the Interior (Minchengpu)]
table.caption_extra: Ministry of the Interior (Minchengpu). The Ministry contains two secretarial departments, and five departments whose duties are respectively to supervise and control:

rows: Local municipal administration, census, promotion of public morality, and matters relating to landlords and tenants.
The training of police, and general supervision of their work.
The measurement and survey of estates, demarcation of boundaries, etc.
Supervision of architectural work, public works and the preservation of ancient buildings and monuments.
Public sanitation, the prevention of plague, examination of doctors and inspection of hospitals.

transcriber_notes: Five departments listed, matching the headnote.
